topic: Research: Google ADK Multi-Agent Guide: Build Agent Teams with A2A Protocol

key_points: CrewAI positions itself as a Python-native framework for collaborative autonomous agents with crews/flows and event-driven control.
The README highlights enterprise-oriented capabilities: tracing/observability, unified control plane, workflow governance, and deployment options (cloud/on-prem).
It advertises fast onboarding and a large community, but this is a vendor-led framing rather than a protocol-level interoperability approach.
LangGraph is explicitly a low-level orchestration runtime for long-running, stateful agents.
Core benefits emphasize persistence, human-in-the-loop controls, and persistent state across sessions.
Docs emphasize using LangGraph when teams need explicit graph/routing control and durable workflows.
AutoGen advertises event-driven multi-agent programming with message passing and local/distributed runtimes.
The stack supports both a Core API (power user control) and AgentChat API (faster prototyping, group chat/two-agent patterns).
Python support and migration guidance indicate a mature, production-oriented ecosystem.
OpenAI presents Agents as workflow-first systems with visual builder and SDK paths for code-defined orchestration.
The platform story emphasizes traceability/evaluation tools for workflow improvement and monitorability.
Agent handoffs are a built-in pattern for decomposing tasks into specialized agents.
Agents SDK focuses on specialized-agent handoff and full trace visibility for debugging execution flow.
SDK-first users can run agents programmatically with tool use, delegation and partial-result streaming.
Repository references show the SDK is maintained as a core OpenAI-native option for production agent apps.

stats.fact: a2aproject/A2A had 24,244 GitHub stars and 2,459 forks (updated 2026-06-12) as a public indicator of ecosystem interest.
google/adk-python had 20,076 GitHub stars and 3,554 forks as of 2026-06-12, reflecting fast adoption of ADK Python adoption.
CrewAI showed 53,294 stars and 7,455 forks, while langchain-ai/langgraph reported 34,485 stars and 5,791 forks on 2026-06-12.
microsoft/autogen was at 58,887 stars and 8,888 forks on 2026-06-12, making it one of the most starred non-trivial OSS agent frameworks in this benchmark set.
ADK docs list ADK Python 2.0 GA as live with graph workflows and collaborative agents, reinforcing its current maturity in Google’s ecosystem.

angles: Position ADK as the natural choice for teams already invested in Google tooling, while using A2A to escape framework lock-in by exposing agent cards and remote A2A-compatible endpoints.
Treat A2A as an interoperability transport, not a replacement for orchestration: ADK still owns internal flow design while A2A handles cross-framework delegation and discovery.
Use ADK's growth path from single-agent to workflows to justify moving incrementally: only split into teams when instruction-following quality, context depth, and modularity pressure appear.

Compare observability and governance features (LangGraph memory/HITL, OpenAI evals, CrewAI control-plane claims, AutoGen distributed events) against Google ADK's traces, callbacks, and session/memory tooling.
Highlight practical architecture choices for 2026: when to deploy hierarchical agent trees vs specialized micro-agents; what to centralize in ADK vs externalize through A2A.
